source_batch.unit_label: Module A unit 9: International Financial Service Centres, GIFT City

facts.statement: An International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) caters to customers outside the jurisdiction of the domestic economy and deals in cross-border flows of finance, products and services: fund raising for individuals, corporates and governments; asset management and global portfolio diversification by pension, insurance and mutual funds; wealth management; global tax management; regional corporate treasury operations; risk management such as insurance and reinsurance; and mergers and acquisitions among transnational corporations. Banks in an IFSC operate like foreign banks located in the home country and are not subject to domestic reserve requirements on deposits; they seek deposits from non-residents and lend to non-residents, and may lend in foreign currency to resident corporates for trade transactions.

The Special Economic Zones Act 2005 allows an IFSC to be set up in a special economic zone or as one after Central Government approval, which makes the zone a testing ground for financial sector reforms; securities transactions entered into by non-residents through an IFSC are exempt from securities transaction tax. The Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, started functioning on 5 December 2019, according to the courseware. The business opportunities listed include access to a large hinterland, a link to the Indian diaspora, wholesale banking, capital markets (trading and clearing members of the IFSC exchanges), retail and private banking, treasury management including non-deliverable forwards, and fund administration.

The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) was set up under the IFSCA Act 2019 as a unified authority for the development and regulation of financial products, services and institutions in the IFSC; before it, the Reserve Bank, SEBI, PFRDA and IRDAI regulated the businesses in the IFSC. The courseware gives 27 April 2020 as its date of establishment and Gandhinagar as its headquarters. The IFSCA (Banking) Regulations, 2020 came into force on 18 November 2020.
facts.locator: Regulations 1(2) and 2; S03 printed p. 245, section 9.5

facts.statement: Indian banks and foreign banks need a licence or permission from the IFSCA to set up a banking unit (BU) in an IFSC. For an IFSC Banking Unit (IBU), which is a branch of the parent bank, the parent must provide capital of at least USD 20 million or such other level as the IFSCA specifies, maintained at the parent bank in the manner specified; obtain a no objection letter from its home regulator; and give an undertaking to provide liquidity to the IBU whenever needed. For an IFSC Banking Company (IBC), a subsidiary of the parent, the parent must provide at least USD 50 million or other specified level and obtain the home regulator's no objection. The courseware (printed pp. 244 and 245) says an eligible Indian bank may set up only one IBU in each IFSC and describes the licence as needing the Reserve Bank's prior permission; the Regulations as amended in 2023 name the IFSCA as the licensing authority.

A banking unit maintains the Liquidity Coverage Ratio and, as and when the IFSCA determines, the Net Stable Funding Ratio, as specified by the IFSCA; an IBU may maintain either at the parent bank with the Authority's prior approval. Leverage ratio and exposure ceiling follow norms the IFSCA specifies (an earlier version fixed the exposure ceiling at 5 per cent of the parent's Tier 1 capital for a single borrower and 10 per cent for a borrower group, replaced on 6 July 2021). The liabilities of an IBU other than deposits from individuals are exempt from the Cash Reserve Ratio or other specified requirements; deposits from individuals are subject to reserve ratios the Authority specifies (the courseware states 3 per cent of deposits as at the end of the previous working day, and exempts IBUs from SLR). Lender of last resort support is not available to a banking unit. An IBU also complies with directions of the home regulator of its parent bank unless the IFSCA specifies otherwise.
facts.locator: Regulations 4(2), 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9; S03 printed pp. 244 and 246

facts.statement: A banking unit conducts business in the specified foreign currencies (as amended, INR business may be allowed subject to settlement in foreign currency) with persons, resident or non-resident, as specified by the Authority. It may open accounts in specified foreign currencies for individuals and corporate or institutional entities, resident in India or outside; resident individuals may hold such accounts for permissible transactions under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme. Cash transactions in these accounts are not permitted; individuals may hold current, savings or term deposit accounts and others current or term deposit accounts. Courseware: IBUs cannot open savings accounts for retail customers in Indian rupees, offer no cheque facility on current accounts, transact by bank transfer, keep separate Nostro accounts, are not allowed to join the Indian domestic call, notice, term and forex markets or payment systems, and may maintain SNRR accounts funded only by foreign currency remittances.
facts.locator: Regulations 10, 11 and 12; S03 printed pp. 246-247, section 9.7

facts.statement: A banking unit may undertake any or all activities mentioned in the IFSCA Act and Section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, except those expressly prohibited by the home regulator of the parent bank or by the IFSCA, subject to the Authority's terms and conditions; providing referral services is permitted. The earlier regulation listed the activities: lending, trade finance, acceptances and guarantees, credit enhancement and credit insurance; inter-bank borrowing and lending; investments; post-shipment export credit in foreign currency and factoring and forfaiting of export receivables; equipment and aircraft leasing; derivatives including non-deliverable forwards; acting as a foreign portfolio investor; and acting as a trading or professional clearing member. A banking unit follows the anti-money laundering and know your customer guidelines of the IFSCA.

Relaxations for foreign portfolio investors at GIFT City, per the courseware: SEBI allows FPIs registered in India to trade on exchanges operating in GIFT City, including commodity derivatives; companies pay no securities transaction tax or commodity transaction tax; exchanges work 22 hours a day; short term capital gains tax on derivatives trade is waived; and retail investors are allowed to trade to build liquidity.

payload.title: What an international financial services centre is
payload.core_explanation_md:
An **IFSC** serves **customers outside the domestic economy**: it handles cross-border **finance, products and services**.

**Typical business**: raising funds for individuals, corporates and governments; **asset management and portfolio diversification** for pension, insurance and mutual funds; **wealth management**; **global tax management**; **regional corporate treasury**; **insurance and reinsurance**; **mergers and acquisitions** among transnational firms.

**Banks in an IFSC** work **like foreign banks sitting in the home country**:
- **Not subject to domestic reserve requirements** on deposits.
- Take deposits from **non-residents**, lend to **non-residents**.
- May lend **in foreign currency to resident corporates for trade**.

payload.title: GIFT City and why a special economic zone
payload.core_explanation_md:
The **SEZ Act, 2005** lets an **IFSC** be set up **inside an SEZ** (or as one) with **Central Government approval**. Because India still restricts parts of its financial sector (partial capital account convertibility, SLR, limits on foreign investment), an SEZ works as a **testing ground** for reforms before they spread.

**Tax**: securities transactions by **non-residents through an IFSC** are **exempt from securities transaction tax**.

**GIFT City**: **Gujarat International Finance Tec-City**, **Gandhinagar**, **started functioning on 5 December 2019** (courseware).

**Opportunities listed**: wholesale banking (**ECB, trade finance, factoring and forfaiting, guarantees, leasing**), **capital markets**, **private and retail banking** (structured and foreign currency deposits), **treasury** (ALM, derivatives, **NDF**), fund administration, and regional offices.

payload.title: IFSCA: one regulator for the centre
payload.core_explanation_md:
**IFSCA** is the **unified regulator** for financial products, services and institutions in the IFSC, created by the **IFSCA Act, 2019**. Before it, the **RBI, SEBI, PFRDA and IRDAI** each regulated their own segments there.

- **Established**: **27 April 2020** (courseware); **headquarters Gandhinagar**.
- **Banking rules**: the **IFSCA (Banking) Regulations, 2020** **came into force on 18 November 2020**.

The aim is **inter-regulatory coordination**, easy doing of business and a **world-class regulatory environment** for an international financial platform.

payload.title: Setting up a banking unit: licence, capital and conditions
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Who licenses**: the **IFSCA** (Indian and foreign banks both need its licence or permission). The courseware says an **eligible Indian bank may open only one IBU in each IFSC**, and mentions RBI permission; the **Regulations as amended in 2023 name the IFSCA**.

| Form | What it is | Minimum capital from parent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **IBU** (IFSC Banking Unit) | a **branch** of the parent | **USD 20 million** (or as IFSCA specifies), **kept at the parent** |
| **IBC** (IFSC Banking Company) | a **subsidiary** | **USD 50 million** (or as specified) |

**Parent bank must also**: get a **no objection letter** from its **home regulator**; give an **undertaking to provide liquidity** to the IBU whenever needed. A foreign bank **without a presence in India** meets **additional requirements**.

payload.title: Prudential rules for an IFSC banking unit
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **Liquidity**: **LCR** and (when determined) **NSFR** as the IFSCA specifies. An **IBU may keep them at the parent bank with the Authority's prior approval**.
- **Leverage ratio and exposure ceiling**: **as the IFSCA specifies**. (The early rule of **5% of the parent's Tier 1** for one borrower and **10%** for a group was **replaced in July 2021**.)
- **Reserves**: liabilities of an IBU **other than deposits from individuals** are **exempt from CRR** (and the courseware says from **SLR**); **individuals' deposits** carry **reserve ratios the Authority sets** (the courseware says **3%** of the previous day's deposits).
- **No lender of last resort** support.
- An IBU also follows **directions of the parent bank's home regulator**, unless the IFSCA says otherwise.

payload.title: What an IFSC banking unit may do
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Currency**: business in **specified foreign currencies**; INR business only where allowed, **settled in foreign currency**.

**Accounts**: foreign currency accounts for **residents and non-residents**, individuals and entities; **residents** may hold them for permissible **LRS** transactions. **No cash transactions**; individuals may hold **current, savings or term deposit** accounts, others **current or term deposit** only. (Courseware: **no cheque facility**, transfers by **bank transfer**, **no Indian rupee savings accounts**, **separate Nostro accounts**, **no access to the domestic call, notice, term, forex and payment systems**, **SNRR accounts** funded only by **foreign currency remittances**.)

**Activities**: **any activity** in the IFSCA Act and **section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act**, **unless prohibited** by the **home regulator** or the **IFSCA**; **referral services** are allowed. The earlier list named **lending and trade finance, guarantees, investments, factoring and forfaiting, aircraft leasing, derivatives including NDFs, acting as an FPI, trading and clearing member**.

**AML/KYC**: follow the **IFSCA's** guidelines.

payload.title: Relaxations for foreign portfolio investors at GIFT City
payload.core_explanation_md:
Per the courseware:

- **SEBI** lets **FPIs registered in India** trade on exchanges in **GIFT City**, including **commodity derivatives**.
- **No securities transaction tax or commodity transaction tax**.
- Exchanges work **22 hours a day**.
- **Short term capital gains tax on derivatives trade is waived** (otherwise 30% for FPIs, as the book states).
- **Retail investors** may trade to build liquidity.

The tax points are the courseware's account and were not checked against the Income-tax Act.

payload.title: Capital still to be brought in for a banking unit
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a parent bank has so far provided USD 14.5 million to its IFSC banking unit, which is a branch. It then decides to convert the arrangement into a subsidiary IFSC banking company instead. How much more must it provide to meet each minimum?

worked_steps.description: Shortfall against the IBU minimum of USD 20 million.
Shortfall against the IBC minimum of USD 50 million.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: USD 5.5 million more for an IBU, or USD 35.5 million more for an IBC

self_check.prompt_text: Where must the parent maintain the capital provided for an IBU?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At the parent bank, in the manner the IFSCA specifies.

unresolved: The courseware's IFSC details follow the 2020 form of the regulations. Where the IFSCA (Banking) Regulations as amended up to 14 July 2023 differ (exposure ceiling, retail reserve ratio, licensing authority, IFSC Banking Company, activities), the cards state the amended text and flag the courseware. Amendments after July 2023 were not searched for.

The IFSCA's directions on specified currencies, reserve ratios, exposure norms and permitted business by segment were not retrieved, so numerical norms beyond the Regulations (such as the 3 per cent reserve ratio and exposure ceilings) are not tested.

The date of GIFT City starting operations, the number of companies and the tax relaxations for foreign portfolio investors are the courseware's statements and were not verified; the tax points are not tested as current law.
The courseware attributes IBU permission to the Reserve Bank; the 2023 Regulations name the IFSCA, which the batch follows.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.

The earlier list named **lending and trade finance, guarantees, investments, factoring and forfaiting, aircraft leasing, derivatives including NDFs, acting as an FPI, trading and clearing member**.

**AML/KYC**: follow the **IFSCA's** guidelines.

items.title: Relaxations for foreign portfolio investors at GIFT City
items.core_explanation_md:
Per the courseware:

- **SEBI** lets **FPIs registered in India** trade on exchanges in **GIFT City**, including **commodity derivatives**.
- **No securities transaction tax or commodity transaction tax**.
- Exchanges work **22 hours a day**.
- **Short term capital gains tax on derivatives trade is waived** (otherwise 30% for FPIs, as the book states).
- **Retail investors** may trade to build liquidity.

The tax points are the courseware's account and were not checked against the Income-tax Act.

items.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a parent bank has so far provided USD 14.5 million to its IFSC banking unit, which is a branch. It then decides to convert the arrangement into a subsidiary IFSC banking company instead. How much more must it provide to meet each minimum?

worked_steps.description: Shortfall against the IBU minimum of USD 20 million.

items.final_answer_with_unit: USD 5.5 million more for an IBU, or USD 35.5 million more for an IBC
